organizations.normalization_notes: The employer name is preserved as spoken by Edward W. Barrett in the 1974 oral history. No modern ownership or successor relationship is inferred.

affiliations.date_precision: The Truman Library's biographical header dates Barrett's COI cable-wireless role from March through June 1942. In the first-person transcript, Barrett says he was Newsweek's national affairs editor, accepted the COI position, and remained only long enough to train a successor. Exact employment dates are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: Newsweek is both the explicit immediate affiliation before Barrett entered Donovan's COI and his last identified civilian employer before that wartime government assignment. COI was the predecessor organization represented by the indexed file; the source then distinguishes his non-clandestine section's June 1942 transfer to OWI.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Edward W. Barrett is high-confidence matched to journalist Edward Ware Barrett, whose first-person oral history documents civilian service in Donovan's Coordinator of Information.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I was working at Newsweek, where I was national affairs editor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, civilian status, Newsweek role, and direct service in Donovan's COI align with the indexed blank-rank Box 39 record.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact Edward W. Barrett name plus multiple corroborating anchors beyond the name: employment at Newsweek, civilian service in Donovan's COI, and a 1942 wartime transition. The personnel file and any identifier remain unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official oral-history header dates COI service to March-June 1942, and the first-person transcript explicitly sequences Newsweek employment, COI recruitment, and the later transfer of the non-clandestine section to OWI.
claims.match_notes: The match remains high confidence rather than confirmed pending Box 39 comparison. The Washington Post obituary calls the 1942 destination OSS, while Princeton's memorial compresses the transition into OWI; the first-person Truman Library transcript supplies the more precise COI-to-OWI sequence.

claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate. The first-person account directly sequences COI hiring, a short handoff period at Newsweek, and departure for Washington; the official header dates the COI role from March 1942.
